subject: Next steps: Procurement path & PR creation guidance (Coupa/Ariba)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@helioshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Procurement path & PR creation guidance (Coupa/Ariba)

Hi Alicia / Ben —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciated the context on your integration timeline and compliance needs. Per our discussion, next steps to get to a pilot:

- Confirm procurement path (PO vs card vs marketplace)
- Help you with PR/PO creation and supplier registration in Coupa/Ariba
- Get any required vendor paperwork to your procurement team (W-9 / legal name / SOW)

Couple of quick clarifications I promised to follow up on:
1) Payment: For an enterprise pilot, we typically accept PO (preferred) or ACH/credit card for smaller pilot purchase. If Helios prefers marketplace (e.g., AWS Marketplace), we can evaluate that path but it usually adds time to procurement.
2) Supplier registration: You mentioned Coupa — do you have an existing vendor ID for "Redwood Inference"? If not, I'll attach a supplier form and a short PR creation guide that your procurement team can use.

I've attached a short PR creation checklist and the Coupa supplier form. Ben — could you confirm who on your side will own the PR creation and whether you need a vendor legal name or tax docs from us?

Happy to jump on a short call with procurement if that's helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Redwood_PR_Instructions.pdf, Coupa_Supplier_Form.xlsx

From: Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@helioshealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@helioshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Procurement path & PR creation guidance (Coupa/Ariba)

Thanks Marissa — good recap.

Quick answers:
- Helios procurement typically issues POs for pilots > $10k. Smaller pilots can be put on a corporate card, but the Approval workflow favors a PO.
- We use Coupa for vendor onboarding and need a supplier registration + W-9 before creating a PR. If Redwood already has a vendor ID in Coupa, that speeds things up.
- I can own the PR creation but will need the vendor legal name, remit address, and a point of contact for invoicing.

I'll kick off the supplier request on our side once I have the vendor details. If you can send the W-9 and the SOW, that'll help.

Ben
Procurement Manager | Helios Health
ben.thompson@helioshealth.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: Procurement path & PR creation guidance (Coupa/Ariba)

Thanks Ben — sending over the requested details.

Vendor legal name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
Remit/Invoice address: 1201 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103
Tax: W-9 attached (Redwood_W9.pdf)
Primary AP contact: invoices@redwood.com

Attached is a short PR creation checklist that maps to Coupa fields (line items, GL codes, contract reference). I also attached the SOW we discussed. If it helps, I can hop on a 15-min screen share with your Coupa admin to walk through the supplier request flow.

A couple of notes on commercial path options:
- PO path: fastest for enterprise procurement and straightforward invoicing.
- Card: works for small pilots but requires an expense reconciliation step.
- Marketplace: we can support AWS Marketplace, but it often requires additional procurement approvals and can add 2–4 weeks.

If you want, loop your Coupa admin and I'll schedule a short session today or Monday.

Cheers,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_SOW-v1.pdf, Redwood_W9.pdf, Redwood_PR_Instructions.pdf
